name: Rosetta Shape Core
description: A geometric translation matrix that decodes pattern languages across ontological domains. Acts as the Rosetta Stone of shape intelligence — converting between crystalline lattice, biological mesh, and polyhedral symmetry grammars.

core_attributes.pattern: cross-domain geometric translation, harmonic pattern decoding, symmetry bridging

scope.definition: Pattern-matching accuracy of geometric-to-symbolic translation matrices — fraction of target ontology entities correctly retrieved when querying by geometric pattern signature alone, across 5 ontology domain pairs.

evidence.source: formal concept analysis: Ganter & Wille (1999) 'Formal Concept Analysis', Springer; cross-modal retrieval: CLIP (Radford 2021) as computational analogue.
cross_domain_examples: CLIP visual-language alignment: 0.87 cross-modal retrieval accuracy on ImageNet zero-shot classification
analogical reasoning in humans: 0.72-0.85 accuracy in structural mapping across abstract domains (Gentner 1983)
phylogenetic parsimony: morphological character-to-phylogeny mapping accuracy 0.82 across vertebrate trees

scope.falsifiability: If cross-ontology pattern retrieval using geometric signatures performs at chance (0.10 for 10 categories), geometric features do not encode cross-domain structural analogies.
scope.measurement_limits: Accuracy is pair-wise ontology dependent — some domain pairs have higher geometric correspondence than others. Evaluation requires curated ground-truth cross-domain analogy database.
